question: A 24-year-old woman presents to the emergency department after she was found agitated and screaming for help in the middle of the street. She says she also has dizziness and tingling in the lips and hands. Her past medical history is relevant for general anxiety disorder, managed medically with paroxetine. At admission, her pulse is 125/min, respiratory rate is 25/min, and body temperature is 36.5°C (97.7°C). Physical examination is unremarkable. An arterial blood gas sample is taken. Which of the following results would you most likely expect to see in this patient?

options.opa: pH: increased, HCO3- : decreased, Pco2: decreased
options.opb: pH: decreased, HCO3- : decreased, Pco2: decreased
options.opc: pH: decreased, HCO3- : increased, Pco2: increased
options.opd: pH: increased, HCO3- : increased, Pco2: increased
options.ope: pH: normal, HCO3- : increased, Pco2: increased

reasoning_chain: CHAIN: Anxiety disorder -> increased sympathetic activity -> tachycardia and tachypnea -> respiratory alkalosis -> decreased Pco2 -> increased pH -> decreased HCO3- -> 85% CHAIN: Paroxetine use -> potential side effect of serotonin syndrome -> agitation and altered mental status -> respiratory alkalosis -> decreased Pco2 -> increased pH -> decreased HCO3- -> 80% CHAIN: Hyperventilation due to anxiety -> respiratory alkalosis -> decreased Pco2 -> increased pH -> decreased HCO3- -> 85%
analysis: The patient is presenting with symptoms of respiratory alkalosis, which is characterized by a decreased Pco2 and an increased pH. This is likely due to hyperventilation, which can be a manifestation of anxiety disorders.
